mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over a 36-month window, no significant negative 20-day forward return occurs after such Fed Funds Rate spikes when inflation is below 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% coincident with a falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% AND UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Early stage of labor market recovery after a recession
failure_condition: In 10 such labor-market turning points since 2000, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the prior month's (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 5% signals weakening demand, which predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market participants anticipate profit compression.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥5% AND RSAFS decreases by ≥5% in the same month
regime_hint: Structural demand weakness in the housing and consumer discretionary sectors
failure_condition: During three such demand shocks since 2008, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 3% while CPIAUCSL (CPI) remains flat for two consecutive months indicates supply-side acceleration that typically precedes a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >3% AND CPIAUCSL is flat for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early phase of a supply-chain loosening
failure_condition: Across 10 such supply expansions since 1990, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than baseline (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months in a context of rising FEDFUNDS (above 3%) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower real rates incentivize equity investment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 3.0% in the same period
failure_condition: In 8 such policy regimes since 1980, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 2% followed by a sharp drop in PAYEMS by 3% within the same quarter is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as profit margin compression outweighs GDP growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥2% in a quarter AND PAYEMS decreases by ≥3% in the same quarter
regime_hint: Economic expansion with sudden labor market softening
failure_condition: During 5 such GDP spikes since 1990, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (GDP) of 4% accompanied by a simultaneous drop in HOUST by 6% signals demand-driven inflationary pressure, which tends to produce a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥4% AND HOUST decreases by ≥6% in the same month
regime_hint: Demand acceleration in a housing-sensitive economy
failure_condition: In 7 such demand surges since 2000, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in both INDPRO and RSAFS by at least 4% in the absence of a parallel CPIAUCSL increase indicates persistent supply-side weakness that predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥4% for two consecutive months AND RSAFS decreases by ≥4% in the same period AND CPIAUCSL does not increase in those months
regime_hint: Structural supply constraints without price inflation
failure_condition: During 6 such supply contractions since 1980, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (IC > 0.10).
